\section{Results}
As shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:pot}, the crater floor charges more negatively as the crater radius increases.
For a radius of 10$\lambda_D$, the floor potential reaches \floorPot{}~V.
Notably, this trend saturates when the radius exceeds the photoelectron sheath thickness.
Overall, these results highlight the pivotal importance of topography for surface charging.

\begin{figure}
\centering
\includegraphics{pot/pot}
\caption{Floor potential versus crater radius. The floor becomes more negative for larger craters.}
